verdict.label: apparent_contradiction
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report an association between circulating irisin and fasting plasma glucose, so the exposure and outcome are comparable. Study A (T2DM patients, cross-sectional) reports that irisin decreased as FPG increased (inverse association, sentence 4). Study B (Taiwanese schoolchildren, cross-sectional) reports a positive irisin–FPG relationship in girls after age adjustment (r = 1.49, P = .038, sentence 8). These directions are opposite. The abstracts supply a concrete, relevant contextual difference: study A examines adults with type 2 diabetes (with or without MAFLD), while study B examines healthy schoolchildren aged 10.3 ± 1.5 years, and study B itself notes the relationship differs by gender ('The contrary relationship between irisin and FPG in boys and girls needs further exploration', sentence 12). This population difference could explain the discrepancy, so apparent_contradiction with factor population is appropriate rather than contradictory.

source_evidence.quote: In T2DM patients, the level of omentin-1 decreased as the level of fasting plasma glucose (FPG) increased and the level of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) reduced; the level of irisin decreased as the levels of FPG and fasting insulin (FINS) increased.
In girls, after adjusting for age, the irisin levels were positively related only to FPG (r = 1.49, P = .038).
There were 376 children (179 boys and 197 girls), aged 10.3 ± 1.5 years, were enrolled.
The contrary relationship between irisin and FPG in boys and girls needs further exploration.

diagnostics.notes: Extraction checks: side A correctly extracts the inverse irisin–FPG association in T2DM patients (estimate_direction '-', sentence 4); side B correctly extracts the positive irisin–FPG association in girls after age adjustment (estimate_direction '+', sentence 8). Comparability: same exposure (circulating irisin) and same outcome (fasting plasma glucose), both cross-sectional association analyses, so the contrast is identifiable. Decision order: both report directional effects with opposite signs, and neither reports an explicit no-effect conclusion, so not_replicated does not apply. The abstracts support a concrete contextual difference — adult T2DM patients (study A) versus healthy schoolchildren in Taiwan with gender-specific associations (study B) — which could explain the opposite directions, yielding apparent_contradiction with factor population.
